correctness.rationale: An explicit two-point remote insertion adds the first missing target once while creating no repeated cross difference; it therefore extends every finite seed with exactly the max(1,d_F) difference counts. Extracting all endpoints for exceptional difference representations leaves at most 2R vertices. In the graph of prescribed S-difference edges, component diameter is at most W. No two different components can share any positive internal distance: their parallel cross pairs would duplicate a cross difference not in S. Repositioning components by H*4^i gives pairwise distinct and H-separated cross-component centers, so all cross differences are unique; within each pair uniqueness follows from disjoint internal difference supports. Each component stays within W of its center, giving the explicit B bound. Finite subsets of [1,B] supply a terminating decision search; a three-term progression realizes a double singleton defect, while three starts of u-pairs force a repeated non-u distance. Python standard-library insertion tests (4 singleton targets times 3 bounds) and randomized 360-case and exhaustive 808-case finite compression checks all passed. Computation is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The source paper arXiv:2610.27786v1 proves existence with many multiplicity-at-least-two indices and gives the singleton multiplicity-three obstruction, but it does not resolve the complementary finitely supported excess regime or give an explicit finite-bounded decision criterion. The 2006 perfect difference construction covers everywhere-one profiles, not mixed finite defects; Lev 2004 chiefly treats partitions into perfect difference sets. Targeted published mathematics index and bibliographic searches did not retrieve the bounded finite-exception inverse theorem. The inference is based on inspected statements and proofs, not mere title matching. A possibility of unindexed or implicitly known elementary compression is retained as a priority risk.
residual_risks: The decision theorem is elementary in spirit and could be implicit in older literature or an unindexed manuscript, despite the explicit absence from the inspected direct sources.
Lev (2004) was checked at abstract level rather than a full-page proof comparison; this is a limited-access coverage uncertainty, not a conclusion of noncoverage.
The finite bound is effective but astronomically large; practical computation and optimality were not claimed.

value.rationale: The October 2026 direct paper singles out finite-support obstruction through its f(1)=3 example while its existence conditions require abundant higher-multiplicity positions. A general bounded finite-certificate theorem resolves the qualitative recognition problem for every finitely supported excess function and recovers an exact singleton classification, with mathematical relevance to inverse additive representation problems. It does not assert computational efficiency, novel density bounds, or a stronger general representation theorem.
